title: Release-prep must also read lore-cli's CHANGELOG by ref: a breaking marker in either repo forces the pair past a patch bump
description:
QCLI-328 (opum-ai/quest-cli#367, squash bee1636) built the per-repository half of opum-doc ADR gate-release-prep-on-a-breaking-changelog-entry-at-a-patch-bump (Decision paragraph 1). scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs reads quest's own CHANGELOG only.

The ADR's Consequences paragraph goes further. Lore and quest share one version (constitution Article 3 clause 1), so a breaking marker in EITHER repository's CHANGELOG forces the pair's bump to at least minor. The check must therefore run against both CHANGELOGs before either side's release proceeds. That includes the repository that "did not change functionally" in the release. Today a breaking entry in lore-cli's CHANGELOG would let quest ship the pair at a patch number.

Orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-28, in a cross-session message to quest-cli: KEEP (QCLI-328) did NOT cover this. File it as a follow-up. It slots after QCLI-331 unless the pair release comes first. lore-cli gets the mirror ruling on LCLI-632 AC3. The ADR is the binding record. The message is the routing.

Scope: quest's release-prep also reads lore-cli's CHANGELOG notes for the paired version BY REF, and applies the same marker-vs-patch rule. The ref is lore-cli dev through the GitHub API, or the paired release ref. The notes are `## Unreleased`, or `## <version>` once finalized. The check FAILS CLOSED when lore's CHANGELOG cannot be read.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest's release-prep reads lore-cli's CHANGELOG by ref, through the GitHub API on lore-cli dev or the paired release ref. It applies the same `### ... (breaking)` marker vocabulary and patch-bump rule as scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs, so a breaking heading in lore's notes for the paired version refuses a patch-level bump of the pair.

When lore's CHANGELOG cannot be read (a 404, an auth failure, a network error, or no parseable version section), the check FAILS with a message naming that cause. It never passes because nothing was read.

Proven as separate measurements on one quest tree: a lore CHANGELOG with a breaking heading refuses the patch bump and accepts a minor bump, and an unreadable lore source refuses. The same run shows the quest-only check unchanged.
The check's output names the lore ref it read and how many lore CHANGELOG sections it read, so a clean result can be told apart from an empty read.
